# Vault — role-aware document access enforced by the database (TypeScript)

## Background

`/home/user/vault` is a small "Vault" document-collaboration project backed by a **local Gel 6.11 instance** (the directory already holds `gel.toml`, the migrated schema in `dbschema/default.gel` and its migration history, and the branch `main` is already seeded with actors, workspaces, memberships and documents).

Right now the database is wide open: any connected client can read and write every row, and there is no application code at all. Product wants the *database itself* to decide what each actor may see and change, and a TypeScript command-line service that talks to it with the correct actor context.

## Requirements

### 1. Actor context

Introduce a schema-level global named exactly `current_actor_id` of type `uuid`. It must be optional: when it is not set, the connection is **anonymous**.

### 2. Rules enforced inside the database

The following rules must be enforced by object-level access policies in the schema, so that **any** client that sets `current_actor_id` (not only your CLI) observes exactly this behaviour. Filtering inside application queries is not acceptable.

Let *A* be the actor identified by `current_actor_id`.

**`Document` — read (select):** *A* may read a document only if *A* has a `Membership` (any role) in the document's workspace or is the document's `owner`. In addition, an **archived** document (`archived := true`) is readable **only** by its `owner`, whatever memberships other actors hold.

**`Document` — create (insert):** allowed only if *A* holds an `Owner` or `Editor` membership in the new document's workspace **and** the new document's `owner` is *A* itself. Inserting a document owned by somebody else must be rejected by the database.

**`Document` — modify (update):** allowed only if *A* may read the document **and** *A* holds an `Owner` or `Editor` membership in the document's workspace. After the update the same condition must still hold for the document's (possibly new) workspace, so a document can never end up in a workspace where *A* is not an `Owner`/`Editor` member.

**`Document` — delete:** allowed only to the document's `owner`.

**`Workspace` — read:** *A* may read only the workspaces *A* is a member of.

**`Membership` — read:** *A* may read only *A*'s own membership rows.

**`Actor` — read:** *A* may read *A*'s own row and the rows of actors who share at least one workspace with *A*.

An anonymous connection (global unset) must be able to read nothing at all from `Document`, `Workspace`, `Membership` and `Actor`, including through nested shapes, link traversal and backlinks.

`ActivityLog` must stay unrestricted (any connection may read and append rows). Write access to `Actor`, `Workspace` and `Membership` is never needed — the service never modifies them, and the existing seed rows must all still be present when you are done.

### 3. Migration

The schema change must be captured as a new migration in `dbschema/migrations/` and applied to the running branch, leaving the branch in sync with `dbschema/default.gel`. The existing migration must not be edited or removed, and no seeded row may be deleted.

### 4. The `vault` command-line service

Implement the service in TypeScript under `/home/user/vault/src/`, split into at least:

* `/home/user/vault/src/service.ts` — the database access layer,
* `/home/user/vault/src/cli.ts` — argument parsing and output.

`npm run build` must compile the TypeScript sources into `/home/user/vault/dist/`, and the resulting CLI must be runnable as `node dist/cli.js <subcommand> [options]` from `/home/user/vault`. Every npm dependency you need is already installed in `/home/user/vault/node_modules`; do not rely on downloading anything else.

Subcommands and their options:

```
node dist/cli.js list-documents  [--actor <email>]
node dist/cli.js read-document   [--actor <email>] --title <title>
node dist/cli.js create-document  --actor <email> --workspace <name> --title <title> --body <body>
node dist/cli.js update-document  --actor <email> --title <title> --body <body>
node dist/cli.js move-document    --actor <email> --title <title> --to-workspace <name>
node dist/cli.js delete-document  --actor <email> --title <title>
node dist/cli.js audit
```

Omitting `--actor` means the command runs anonymously. `audit` takes no options and must list **every** document stored in the branch, ignoring all object-level rules.

## Implementation Hints

* Project path: `/home/user/vault` (run every command from there).
* The local Gel server (Gel 6.11, branch `main`) may not be running yet; `/usr/local/bin/start-gel.sh` starts it if needed and returns once the branch accepts queries. It is safe to run repeatedly.
* Connection settings for that instance are already exported in the environment, so both the `gel` CLI and the `gel` npm client connect without extra configuration.
* Command: `node dist/cli.js <subcommand> [options]`, after `npm run build`.
* Every invocation must print **exactly one line of JSON to stdout** and nothing else on stdout (diagnostics, if any, go to stderr).
* On success print `{"ok": true, "actor": <email or null>, "action": "<subcommand>", "data": <payload>}` and exit with code `0`.
* On failure print `{"ok": false, "actor": <email or null>, "action": "<subcommand>", "error": {"code": "<CODE>", "message": "<non-empty string>"}}` and exit with the code listed below. `actor` echoes the `--actor` value (or `null` when it was omitted); `action` echoes the subcommand name; for an unknown subcommand `action` must be the string that was passed (or `null` if none was passed).
* `data` payloads, with exactly these keys and no others:
  * `list-documents` and `audit`: a JSON array of document objects with the keys `title`, `workspace` (workspace name), `owner_email`, `archived`, sorted by `title` ascending.
  * `read-document`: a single object with the keys `title`, `workspace`, `owner_email`, `archived`, `body`.
  * `create-document`, `update-document`, `move-document`: a single object with the keys `title`, `workspace`, `owner_email`, `archived` describing the document after the operation.
  * `delete-document`: a single object with the only key `title`.
* Error codes and exit codes:
  * `BAD_REQUEST` / exit `2` — unknown subcommand, a missing or empty required option, an `--actor` email that matches no `Actor` row, or a workspace name that matches no `Workspace` row.
  * `NOT_FOUND` / exit `3` — `read-document` found no document with that title that the acting actor is allowed to read.
  * `NO_MATCH` / exit `3` — `update-document`, `move-document` or `delete-document` matched no document the acting actor is allowed to change.
  * `POLICY_VIOLATION` / exit `4` — the database rejected the write because it violates the object-level rules.
  * `CONFLICT` / exit `5` — the write violated a schema constraint (for example a duplicate document title).
* Resolving an `--actor` email or a `--workspace`/`--to-workspace` name to a database object must succeed regardless of what the acting actor is allowed to read; only the document operation itself is subject to the rules above. A write that the rules reject must leave the database unchanged.
* Every command that successfully creates, updates, moves or deletes a document must append exactly one `ActivityLog` row whose `action` is the subcommand name, `actor_email` is the acting actor's email and `doc_title` is the affected document's title. A command that fails must append no `ActivityLog` row, and for `create-document` the new document and its `ActivityLog` row must be committed atomically in a single transaction.

# Verification Plan

## Setup

1. Run `/usr/local/bin/start-gel.sh` and wait until the branch answers queries (every check that touches the database or the CLI must depend on this).
2. `cd /home/user/vault && npm run build` — must exit 0 and (re)produce `dist/cli.js`.
3. With a privileged connection (`configure session set apply_access_policies := false`), delete any leftover `Document` titled `alpha-draft` and any `ActivityLog` row mentioning it, so the checks are re-runnable.

Baseline data seeded at image build time:

* Workspaces: `alpha`, `beta`, `gamma`, `delta`.
* Actors: `ana@vault.test`, `evan@vault.test`, `vera@vault.test`, `bruno@vault.test`, `nomad@vault.test`.
* Memberships: ana/alpha = `Owner`, evan/alpha = `Editor`, vera/alpha = `Viewer`, bruno/beta = `Owner`, ana/gamma = `Editor`, evan/delta = `Viewer`. `nomad@vault.test` has no membership.
* Documents (title / workspace / owner / archived / body): `alpha-roadmap` / alpha / ana / false / `Roadmap v1`; `alpha-notes` / alpha / evan / false / `Notes v1`; `alpha-archive-2019` / alpha / ana / **true** / `Archived plans`; `beta-charter` / beta / bruno / false / `Charter v1`.

"Privileged connection" below means a connection that ignores object-level rules; it is used only by the checks to inspect the true state of the branch. Actor UUIDs are looked up over such a connection and then injected with `set global current_actor_id := <uuid>'…'` (the `gel query` CLI keeps session state across the queries passed in one invocation).

## Verification Steps

1. **Schema shape**: `schema::Global` contains `default::current_actor_id` with target `std::uuid` and `required = false`. The object types `default::Document`, `default::Workspace`, `default::Membership`, `default::Actor` each expose at least one entry in `access_policies`, `default::ActivityLog` exposes none, and the union of `access_kinds` over `default::Document`'s policies is exactly `{Select, Insert, UpdateRead, UpdateWrite, Delete}`.

2. **Migration state**: `gel migration status` (run from `/home/user/vault`) reports the database is up to date, `dbschema/migrations/` holds at least 2 `*.edgeql` files (resolved by globbing — never by a hardcoded hashed filename) and the original `00001-*.edgeql` file is byte-identical to the copy kept at `/opt/vault-baseline/00001.edgeql`.

3. **Seed intact** (privileged): `count(Document)` = 4, `count(Actor)` = 5, `count(Workspace)` = 4, `count(Membership)` = 6, and the four baseline titles are present with their baseline bodies.

4. **Document read visibility straight from the database** (`set global current_actor_id`, then `select Document { title } order by .title`):
   * ana → `["alpha-archive-2019", "alpha-notes", "alpha-roadmap"]`
   * evan → `["alpha-notes", "alpha-roadmap"]`
   * vera → `["alpha-notes", "alpha-roadmap"]`
   * bruno → `["beta-charter"]`
   * nomad → `[]`
   * global unset (anonymous) → `[]`

5. **Workspace / Membership / Actor visibility**, same technique:
   * workspaces: ana → `["alpha", "gamma"]`; evan → `["alpha", "delta"]`; vera → `["alpha"]`; bruno → `["beta"]`; nomad → `[]`; anonymous → `[]`
   * `count(Membership)`: ana → 2; evan → 2; vera → 1; nomad → 0; anonymous → 0
   * actor emails: ana → `["ana@vault.test", "evan@vault.test", "vera@vault.test"]`; bruno → `["bruno@vault.test"]`; nomad → `["nomad@vault.test"]`; anonymous → `[]`

6. **No leakage through traversal / backlinks**:
   * as vera: `select Workspace { name, docs := (select .<workspace[is Document] order by .title).title }` returns exactly one workspace `alpha` whose `docs` are exactly `["alpha-notes", "alpha-roadmap"]` — the archived document never appears.
   * as bruno: `select Document { title, owner_email := .owner.email }` returns only `beta-charter` with `bruno@vault.test`.
   * anonymous: `select Document { title, owner: { email } }` returns `[]`.

7. **Owner spoofing is refused by the database**: with `current_actor_id` set to evan, `insert Document { title := 'spoofed', body := 'x', workspace := (alpha), owner := (ana) }` fails with an `AccessPolicyError`, and no document titled `spoofed` exists afterwards (privileged check).

8. **`list-documents`**: `node dist/cli.js list-documents --actor vera@vault.test` exits 0 and prints one JSON line with `ok=true`, `actor="vera@vault.test"`, `action="list-documents"`, `data` = `[{"title":"alpha-notes","workspace":"alpha","owner_email":"evan@vault.test","archived":false},{"title":"alpha-roadmap","workspace":"alpha","owner_email":"ana@vault.test","archived":false}]` (exactly these keys, this order). With `--actor ana@vault.test` the result has 3 entries starting with `alpha-archive-2019` whose `archived` is true. With `--actor nomad@vault.test` and with no `--actor` at all, `data` is `[]` and `actor` is respectively the email and `null`.

9. **`read-document`**: `--actor vera@vault.test --title alpha-roadmap` exits 0 with `data.body = "Roadmap v1"` and exactly the keys `title`, `workspace`, `owner_email`, `archived`, `body`; `--actor evan@vault.test --title alpha-archive-2019` exits 3 with `error.code = "NOT_FOUND"`; `--actor ana@vault.test --title beta-charter` exits 3 with `NOT_FOUND`; `--title alpha-roadmap` without `--actor` exits 3 with `NOT_FOUND`.

10. **Bad requests**: `read-document --actor ghost@vault.test --title alpha-roadmap` → exit 2, `BAD_REQUEST`; `create-document --actor evan@vault.test --workspace epsilon --title x --body y` → exit 2, `BAD_REQUEST`; `frobnicate --actor evan@vault.test` → exit 2, `BAD_REQUEST` with `action = "frobnicate"`; `update-document --actor evan@vault.test --title alpha-notes` (no `--body`) → exit 2, `BAD_REQUEST`.

11. **Denied create**: `create-document --actor vera@vault.test --workspace alpha --title vera-attempt --body nope` exits 4 with `POLICY_VIOLATION`; afterwards the privileged document count is still 4, no `vera-attempt` document exists, and the number of `ActivityLog` rows is unchanged.

12. **Allowed create is atomic with its log**: `create-document --actor evan@vault.test --workspace alpha --title alpha-draft --body "Draft v1"` exits 0 with `data` = `{"title":"alpha-draft","workspace":"alpha","owner_email":"evan@vault.test","archived":false}`; privileged count becomes 5; exactly one new `ActivityLog` row exists with `action="create-document"`, `actor_email="evan@vault.test"`, `doc_title="alpha-draft"`.

13. **Duplicate title**: repeating the exact same `create-document` call exits 5 with `CONFLICT` and the privileged count stays 5.

14. **Denied update**: `update-document --actor vera@vault.test --title alpha-notes --body hacked` exits 3 with `NO_MATCH`; `update-document --actor evan@vault.test --title alpha-archive-2019 --body hacked` exits 3 with `NO_MATCH`. Privileged reads still show `Notes v1` and `Archived plans`.

15. **Allowed update**: `update-document --actor ana@vault.test --title alpha-notes --body "Notes v2"` exits 0; privileged read of `alpha-notes` shows `Notes v2`; then `update-document --actor ana@vault.test --title alpha-notes --body "Notes v1"` exits 0 and restores the baseline body.

16. **Denied move**: `move-document --actor evan@vault.test --title alpha-notes --to-workspace delta` exits 4 with `POLICY_VIOLATION` and a privileged read still shows `alpha-notes` in `alpha`.

17. **Allowed move + restore**: `move-document --actor ana@vault.test --title alpha-roadmap --to-workspace gamma` exits 0 with `data.workspace = "gamma"` (privileged read confirms `gamma`); `move-document --actor ana@vault.test --title alpha-roadmap --to-workspace alpha` exits 0 and puts it back in `alpha`.

18. **Delete rules**: `delete-document --actor ana@vault.test --title alpha-draft` exits 3 with `NO_MATCH` (ana owns the workspace but not the document) and the document still exists; `delete-document --actor evan@vault.test --title alpha-draft` exits 0 with `data` exactly `{"title": "alpha-draft"}` and the privileged count returns to 4.

19. **Bypass path**: `node dist/cli.js audit` exits 0 with `actor = null` and lists exactly the four baseline titles in ascending order — including `alpha-archive-2019` and `beta-charter` — with their correct `workspace` and `owner_email`.

20. **Activity log accounting**: over the whole run, `ActivityLog` gains rows only for the successful `create-document`, the two `update-document`, the two `move-document` and the `delete-document` calls, each with the matching `actor_email`/`doc_title`, and none for any rejected call.

21. **Source layout**: `/home/user/vault/src/service.ts`, `/home/user/vault/src/cli.ts` and `/home/user/vault/dist/cli.js` exist, and every CLI invocation above prints exactly one line of parseable JSON on stdout.
